commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Cap warmup and CUDA graph sizes to max_num_seqs * max_model_len
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fixes #66244.

When `max_num_batched_tokens > max_num_seqs * max_model_len`, dummy forwards could run with more tokens than a real batch can hold: compile-range warmup, FlashInfer autotune (`_run_flashinfer_autotune_dummy_runs`) and full/mixed CUDA graph capture all size them up to `max_num_batched_tokens`. `InputBatch.make_dummy` spreads those tokens over at most `max_num_reqs` requests, which gives sequences longer than `max_model_len` and out-of-bounds block table access (`CUDA error: an illegal memory access` in FlashAttention).

#67545 caps `_dummy_run`, which covers compile-range warmup and FlashInfer autotune. CUDA graph capture does not go through `_dummy_run`, so this PR limits the capture sizes.

## Changes

- `CudaGraphManager._init_candidates` (`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/cudagraph_utils.py`): drops prefill/mixed capture sizes above `max_num_reqs * max_model_len`, with a warning in the style of the existing "Dropping ... from ..." message.
- Tests: `test_cudagraph_candidates_skip_sizes_exceeding_max_model_len` (`tests/v1/cudagraph/test_cudagraph_manager.py`). The CUDA graph test helpers now set a concrete `max_model_len`.
- An earlier revision also capped `_dummy_run`. dfc2c72 dropped that cap and its test, since #67545 added the same cap.

## Verification

- Reproduced the crash on Colab L4 (`Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct`, `max_model_len=448`, `max_num_batched_tokens=1000`, `max_num_seqs=1`) with `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1` (`_vllm_fa2_C.varlen_fwd` illegal memory access).
- @Pb314314 reproduced #66244 on GB200 with `--attention-backend FLASH_ATTN`, including the FlashInfer autotune path, and confirmed both pass with the earlier revision, whose `_dummy_run` cap gives the same token counts as #67545's.
- Unit tests at dfc2c72: the 22 test files that build a CUDA graph manager or call `_dummy_run` and import in my environment give the same results as `main` (692 passed, 28 skipped, 20 failed; the 20 fail the same way on `main` locally). `test_deepseek_v41_decoder_replay_layers.py` and `test_deepseek_v41_replay_batch.py` need FlashMLA, which my local build lacks.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on the modified files.

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][DeepSeek-V4.1] Enable eager prefill context parallel for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Enables eager prefill context parallelism (PCP) for the text-only DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash model on ROCm, Model Runner V2. This picks up the inactive draft #62981 by @haic0 (kept as co-author) and ports it onto current main.

## Claims

- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash serves with `--prefill-context-parallel-size 2` on ROCm. On main it fails at startup with `NotImplementedError: DeepSeek-V4.1 PCP currently supports NVIDIA CUDA only.`
- GSM8K with TP=2 + PCP=2 lands within about one standard error of the no-PCP baseline. Expert parallel on top of PCP also works.
- MoE routing input IDs are gathered across PCP ranks when expert parallel is off, matching the MoE runner's PCP gather of hidden states.
- PCP attention skips the ROCm stream-overlap path, which caches the compressor latent without the PCP gather, zeroes the PCP-padded output tail, and returns early on a rank with no tokens, as CUDA FlashMLA does.
- Unsupported combinations (PP, DP, DCP, microbatching, spec decode, KV transfer, prefix caching, `aiter_mega_moe`, monokernel) are rejected at startup.
- `fused_compress_quant_cache.py` picks the PCP predecessor row with `tl.where`, which avoids a ROCm Triton compile failure at real cache sizes (triton-lang/triton#12695).
- CI: `test_deepseek_v41_pcp.py` now runs in the MI355 `Basic Models (Other)` mirror. It was not listed there before, so the ROCm CI never ran it.
- Docs: ROCm section in `context_parallel_deployment.md`.

## Validation

MI350X (gfx950), `/data/models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, eager, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`, prefix caching off, on the branch merged with current main.

**GSM8K** (all 1319, 5-shot, greedy):

| Config | repo `gsm8k_eval.py` | lm_eval strict / flexible |
|---|---|---|
| main, TP=2 + PCP=2 | fails at startup | - |
| TP=2 + PCP=2, run 1 | 90.0% | 93.1% / 93.1% |
| TP=2 + PCP=2, run 2 (the new CI config through `test_gsm8k_correctness.py`) | 89.6% | - |
| TP=2 + PCP=2 + EP | 90.1% | - |
| TP=4, no PCP | 91.4% | - |

Before the merge with main, TP=2 + PCP=2 gave 90.5% / 90.4% on the repo harness and TP=2 without PCP gave 90.5%, with lm_eval at 92.3-93.4% for both. TP=2 without PCP no longer fits after the merge (OOM in the MXFP4 MoE weight conversion with 140.65 GiB already used), so the baseline above is TP=4. PCP splits the experts over all four GPUs (81 GiB of weights per GPU), so it is not affected. The PCP-to-baseline gap of 1.4 points is about 1.2 standard errors of the difference at 1319 questions.

The docs command, run as written (default 1M max length), started and answered a 4k-token retrieval prompt correctly.

EP + PCP ran with the `AgRsAll2AllManager`, 96 of 384 experts per rank, and no server errors.

**Tests:**

```bash
pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_pcp.py   # 30 passed, 2 skipped (8-GPU CUDA only); 10/10 runs on 1 GPU
```

The 12 new ROCm cases fail on main and pass here, on one visible GPU and on four. Removing the routing-ID gather, a gate condition, or the `use_pcp` check in the attention forward each makes the matching test fail. pre-commit is clean, incl. mypy.

**Compressor kernel:** with a 2.14 GiB state cache, `_fused_save_compress_norm_kernel` fails to compile on main (`'scf.if' op ... region branch point has 2 operands, but region successor needs 1 inputs`) and compiles here; its output is bit-identical to the small-cache result.

## Details

- **Not a duplicate:** this supersedes #62981, a draft with no activity since 2026-10-27 and no reply to a follow-up on 2026-11-05. No other open PR enables PCP for DeepSeek-V4.1 on ROCm (#66322 adds PCP/DCP to the V3.2/GLM sparse MLA backend and does not touch `deepseek_v41`).
- **CI gap:** the first version of the gate test built a real `ParallelConfig(prefill_context_parallel_size=2)`, which fails on a 1-GPU CUDA agent with `World size (2) is larger than the number of available GPUs (1)`. ROCm CI did not catch it because the MI355 mirror keeps its own file list and never ran `test_deepseek_v41_pcp.py`. On ROCm it would have passed anyway: that world-size check is gated on `is_cuda()`. The test now uses a plain config object, and the file is added to the mirror.
- **Port notes:** the `_prepare_and_attn_*` helpers #62981 touched no longer exist; the V2 runner's PCP manager already rejects CUDA graphs, LoRA and multimodal for this model, so those gates were dropped; the empty-buffer guards in the decode top-k and SWA paths were dropped because an empty rank now returns before reaching them, and the fused packer only runs with the monokernel, which PCP rejects.
- **Triton root cause:** #62981 worked around the compressor failure with `AMDGCN_USE_BUFFER_OPS=0`. ROCm Triton's `CanonicalizePointers` handles an `arith.select` between a >2 GiB pointer and a narrowed one, but not the same merge through `scf.if`; the ring state cache exceeds 2 GiB at real sizes. `tl.where` lowers to the select the pass already handles. Reported as triton-lang/triton#12695.
- **Limitations:** PCP=4 needs eight GPUs at TP=2 and was not run. The `tl.where` change is in a kernel CUDA also runs; it is standard Triton but was not run on NVIDIA.

commits.pr_title: [CI][Test] Patch the platform class, not the instance, in the humming quantization tests
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

`(H200 MIG 35GB) Quantization` Shard 4/4 has failed on every main build since [102780](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/102780), through nightly 102861:

```
FAILED quantization/test_modelopt.py::test_modelopt_nested_mixed_checkpoint - _pickle.PicklingError: Can't pickle <functools._lru_cache_wrapper object at 0x...>: it's not the same object as vllm.platforms.cuda.NvmlCudaPlatform.get_device_capability
FAILED quantization/test_modelopt.py::test_modelopt_mixed_dspark_checkpoint - (same)
```

`test_humming_nvfp4_linear_declares_executed_activation` (from #59460) monkeypatches `get_device_capability` on the `current_platform` *instance*. Before pytest 9.2, undoing an instance patch writes the inherited value back onto the instance. That leaves a bound `@classmethod @cache` method in `current_platform.__dict__`. A later test that sends a closure over `current_platform` through `LLM.apply_model` then fails in cloudpickle, which can't pickle that lru_cache wrapper by reference.

No code change caused this. The step was re-enabled at 102760 (#66672). Once the runtime sharder had timings, it re-split the shards and put `test_humming_mxfp4_block_fp8.py` before `test_modelopt.py` in shard 4.

The fix patches the class (`type(current_platform)`) with a `classmethod` for both patches in that file. Undoing it then restores the original attribute cleanly on any pytest version. This is a test-only change.

## Relation to #67673

#67673 fixes the same leak globally by raising the pin to pytest>=9.2.0 and regenerating 8 requirement locks. This PR is the narrow, test-only fix for the file that leaks. It can land first to turn the step green, and it stays correct after #67673. Either can land without the other.

## Test Plan

- A minimal pytest 9.1.0 + cloudpickle repro: patching the instance reproduces the exact `PicklingError`, and patching the class doesn't.
- CI: `quantization` (H200 MIG 35GB, all shards), as a selected-steps build on this PR.
- `pre-commit run --files tests/quantization/test_humming_mxfp4_block_fp8.py`

## Test Result

- Repro behaves as expected, and pre-commit passes.
- GPU: [build 102870](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/102870), `quantization` (H200 MIG 35GB): all 4 shards passed. In Shard 4/4 `test_humming_mxfp4_block_fp8.py` ran before `test_modelopt.py`, the order that fails on main, and both modelopt tests passed.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; I reviewed the change.
